This position serves as the Pharmacy Manager responsible for leading comprehensive clinical pharmacy services across Acute Care and Transitions of Care. The Manager is accountable for service-line performance, clinical and operational quality, regulatory readiness, medication-use safety, financial stewardship, workforce planning, and staff development. Working closely with the Associate Chief Pharmacy Officer of Inpatient Pharmacy Services, the Assistant Chief Pharmacy Officer of Inpatient Clinical Services, and other Pharmacy Leadership, the Manager identifies improvement opportunities, implements sustainable solutions, advances clinical pharmacy practice, and promotes operational effectiveness and efficiency. The Manager ensures clinical pharmacy services comply with state and federal regulations, Joint Commission standards, professional practice standards, University and department policies, and applicable collective bargaining agreements. The Manager serves as hiring manager and direct supervisor for clinical pharmacists, technician supervisors, and assigned pharmacy personnel within the Acute Care and Transitions of Care pharmacy teams. The Manager also partners with interdisciplinary leaders, Patient Care Services, medical staff, and other departments to support safe medication management, optimize transitions of care, improve patient outcomes, and align pharmacy services with organizational priorities. #CA-DS

Knowledge of pharmacy practice standards, medication use safety principles, formulary management, and transitions of care workflows
Ability to support staff development, performance feedback, conflict resolution, change management, and effective team-based communication in a dynamic health-system environment

Ability to lead operational, clinical, quality improvement, informatics, transitions-of-care, formulary, and medication safety projects using sound project management methods, data-informed decision-making, and effective follow-through

Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to engage frontline staff, pharmacy leadership, interdisciplinary partners, physicians, nurses, case management, discharge planning teams, outpatient pharmacy partners, and other stakeholders
Ability to analyze operational and clinical performance data and implement process improvement

Knowledge of electronic health record, computerized provider order entry, clinical decision support, medication reconciliation, discharge medication workflows, and pharmacy informatics processes sufficient to support safe and efficient medication management
